paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Distribution of articles across political leanings of the outlets
model_annotation: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of articles across the political leanings of the outlets, divided into four distinct categories: “Right bias,” “Left bias,” “Left center bias,” and “Questionable source.” The chart is segmented into four colored slices, each labeled with its category name, percentage value, and corresponding count in parentheses. The “Right bias” category, shown in blue, constitutes the largest portion at 30.0% (30 articles). The “Left bias” category, depicted in orange, accounts for 28.0% (28 articles). The “Questionable source” category, colored green, represents 22.0% (22 articles). The smallest segment, “Left center bias,” shown in red, makes up 20.0% (20 articles). All percentage values and counts are clearly labeled within their respective slices, and there is no legend or visual emphasis such as exploded segments; the slices appear to be arranged in a clockwise descending order by size, starting from the top-right.
